title: S7schema
text: S7schema provides generic way working yaml config files. main functionality captured S7schema() explore vignette.

title: S7schema
text: First find example configuration schema files used demonstrate S7schema(). schema.json defines simple configuration file, consists one entry (my_config_var) single number: initial config.yml defines entry value 1: obviously valid configuration. check programmatically can also use one-shot validation function validate_yaml():
code: ex_config <- system.file("examples/config.yml", package = "S7schema") ex_schema <- system.file("examples/schema.json", package = "S7schema") {   "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema",   "title": "My config schema",   "description": "Simple example schema with one allowed entry",   "type": "object",   "properties": {     "my_config_var": {       "description": "My only configuration variable",       "type": "number"     }   },   "additionalProperties": false } --- my_config_var: 1 validate_yaml(file = ex_config, schema = ex_schema)

title: S7schema
text: Alternatively can load, validate, write configuration S7schema() class. load simple create new S7schema object based config schema files : can see config S7 object, list containing content config.yml. can seen inspecting class: Since list, easy access value my_config_var directly: similarly overwrite value: Note validation automatically triggered updating value, needed call explicitly. also can update illegal entry , get error validating updated object: save configuration use write_config(): just wrapper around yaml::write_yaml(), advantage S7schema input always validated file created.
code: config <- S7schema(file = ex_config, schema = ex_schema) print(config) #> <S7schema::S7schema> List of 1 #>  $ my_config_var: int 1 #>  @ schema   : chr "/home/runner/work/_temp/Library/S7schema/examples/schema.json" #>  @ validator: <S7schema::validator> #>  .. @ context:Classes 'V8', 'environment' <environment: 0x563ccc144e80>  #>  @ file     : chr "/home/runner/work/_temp/Library/S7schema/examples/config.yml" class(config) #> [1] "S7schema::S7schema" "list"               "S7_object" config$my_config_var #> [1] 1 config$my_config_var <- 2 validate(config) print(config) #> <S7schema::S7schema> List of 1 #>  $ my_config_var: num 2 #>  @ schema   : chr "/home/runner/work/_temp/Library/S7schema/examples/schema.json" #>  @ validator: <S7schema::validator> #>  .. @ context:Classes 'V8', 'environment' <environment: 0x563cc863b430>  #>  @ file     : chr "/home/runner/work/_temp/Library/S7schema/examples/config.yml" config$my_config_var <- "abc" validate(config) #> Error in `validate_S7schema()`: #> ! /my_config_var must be number #> ✖ type: number #> ℹ current value: "abc" write_config(   x = config,   path = "my/config.yml" )

title: Use S7schema in your package
text: maintain package requires specific configuration format, S7schema lets define validated config class minimal code. extending S7schema, package gets schema validation, YAML reading/writing, schema documentation free.

title: Use S7schema in your package
text: JSON schema describes structure constraints configuration. real package, schema live inst/ (e.g. inst/schema/my_schema.json) ships package can found via system.file(). vignette use example schema bundled S7schema:
code: schema_path <- system.file("examples/schema.json", package = "S7schema") {   "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema",   "title": "My config schema",   "description": "Simple example schema with one allowed entry",   "type": "object",   "properties": {     "my_config_var": {       "description": "My only configuration variable",       "type": "number"     }   },   "additionalProperties": false }

title: Use S7schema in your package
text: core pattern create S7 class inherits S7schema hard-codes schema path constructor: Users package need supply config file path — schema handled internally.
code: my_config_class <- S7::new_class(   name = "my_config_class",   parent = S7schema::S7schema,   constructor = function(file) {     S7::new_object(       .parent = S7schema::S7schema(         file = file,         schema = system.file("examples/schema.json", package = "S7schema")       )     )   } )

title: Use S7schema in your package
text: Creating instance loads validates YAML file automatically:
code: config_path <- system.file("examples/config.yml", package = "S7schema") x <- my_config_class(file = config_path) print(x) #> <my_config_class> List of 1 #>  $ my_config_var: int 1 #>  @ schema   : chr "/home/runner/work/_temp/Library/S7schema/examples/schema.json" #>  @ validator: <S7schema::validator> #>  .. @ context:Classes 'V8', 'environment' <environment: 0x555fca6cb370>  #>  @ file     : chr "/home/runner/work/_temp/Library/S7schema/examples/config.yml"

code: x$my_config_var <- "not a number" S7::validate(x) #> Error in `validate_S7schema()`: #> ! /my_config_var must be number #> ✖ type: number #> ℹ current value: "not a number"

code: tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".yml") x$my_config_var <- 42 write_config(x, path = tmp) readLines(tmp) #> [1] "my_config_var: 42.0" md <- document_schema(schema_path) cat(md) #> # My config schema #>  #> Simple example schema with one allowed entry #>  #> |Type   |Additional Properties | #> |:------|:---------------------| #> |object |No                    | #>  #> ## Properties #>  #> |Name          |Description                    |Type   |Required | #> |:-------------|:------------------------------|:------|:--------| #> |my_config_var |My only configuration variable |number |No       | md <- document_schema(schema_path, header_start_level = 3) cat(md) #> ### My config schema #>  #> Simple example schema with one allowed entry #>  #> |Type   |Additional Properties | #> |:------|:---------------------| #> |object |No                    | #>  #> #### Properties #>  #> |Name          |Description                    |Type   |Required | #> |:-------------|:------------------------------|:------|:--------| #> |my_config_var |My only configuration variable |number |No       |

title: Work with valid configurations — S7schema
text: S7schema() provides generic way working yaml configuration files. object created supplying initial YAML configuration (file) JSON schema definition (schema) configuration file. initial configuration validated new object returned. valid first error thrown, together path entry YAML file, description error. S7schema class inherits list, ensuring content YAML file can accessed read directly yaml::read_yaml(), supports workflow: Read validate config file: x <- S7schema(...) Edit content list: x$new_entry <- "new_value" Validate new content original schema: validate(x) Use values downstream functions: x$new_entry
